findings.issue_text: [High/bug] packages/core/EventManager.ts:117-118 — Missing optional chaining: `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is accessed without `?.` after `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` destructuring; when destinationCalendar is null (handleNewBooking can set it to null) or [], this throws TypeError in EventManager.create, crashing bookings (e.g. Google Meet location with no destination calendar) instead of falling back to Cal Video.

[High/bug] packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts updateEvent (~253) and deleteEvent (~315) — the fallback `destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is only evaluated in the branch where externalCalendarId is falsy, so the predicate never matches; calendarId/selectedCalendar becomes undefined and googleapis rejects the call with 'Missing required parameter: calendarId', breaking update/delete for references with null/absent externalCalendarId (legacy bookings and the new no-credentialId path).

[High/bug] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts:151 — refactor inverted the condition from `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`; orgs now get slug set directly when team billing is enabled (bypassing the requestedSlug approval flow, which is also set — contradictory) and get no slug at all when billing is disabled.

[Medium/bug] packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:~145-155 — `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"` silently creates the event on the credential's primary calendar when no destinationCalendar entry matches credentialId, causing duplicate events for multi-credential users or events on the wrong account when destination rows have null credentialId; additionally CalendarManager.createEvent echoes back the passed-in externalId even when 'primary' was actually used, so the stored reference points at the wrong calendar.

[Medium/bug] Office365 CalendarService (72-76), Lark CalendarService (127-129), and packages/lib/CalendarService.ts (156-163) — these services read only `destinationCalendar[0].externalId` and ignore the per-credential entry (credentialId param unused), so in the multi-host collective flow each host's credential writes to the first host's calendar externalId causing API errors/404s; the collective multiple host feature effectively only works with Google.

[Medium/bug] packages/core/EventManager.ts:~377-385 — in createAllCalendarEvents, the no-credentialId else branch (filter by integration type + create on every matching credential) now runs once per destination inside the for loop, so two destination entries with the same integration and null credentialId create N×M duplicate events.

[Medium/bug] packages/core/EventManager.ts:~510-535 (updateAllCalendarEvents) — unlike createAllCalendarEvents which guards with `if (credential)`, the update path calls `result.push(updateEvent(credential, ...))` with no guard after the DB lookup fails, so an unresolvable reference.credentialId (deleted credential, missing app slug) passes undefined to updateEvent, throwing and converting all reference updates for the booking into failures.

[Medium/bug] packages/core/EventManager.ts:~552-555 — the newBookingId merge cleanup uses `booking.references.find((reference) => reference.type.includes("_calendar"))` and deletes only the first old calendar reference, so reschedule/merge on bookings created via the multi-destination flow leaves stale events on the other hosts' calendars.

[Medium/bug] packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:~440-470 — the recurring-series deletion block (iterating all of bookingToDelete.user.credentials × updatedBookings, ignoring the loop's reference) is now inside the `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop, executing once per calendar reference causing duplicate delete calls and repeated 404/log noise; it also still only covers the organizer's credentials so other hosts' recurring events are never cleaned up.

[Medium/data] packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:~1871-1877 — only `evt.destinationCalendar[0]` is connected to the booking and there is no schema migration to persist per-host destinations, so later flows that rebuild CalendarEvent from booking.destinationCalendar (confirm.handler.ts, paypal-webhook.ts, webhook.ts handlePaymentSuccess) create calendar events only on the first host's calendar, silently skipping all other hosts' destination calendars for collective bookings requiring payment/confirmation.

[Low/security] packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:~755-760 — loadUsers' catch rethrows Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError messages verbatim as a 400 response, leaking internal database error details to API clients and miscategorizing a server-side failure as a client error.

[Low/bug] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/requestReschedule.handler.ts:239-242 — the original duplicated expression (`bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar || bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar`, missing the intended `|| user.destinationCalendar`) is preserved as `? [bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar] : []` instead of adding the user fallback used consistently in every other handler converted in this PR.

[Low/bug] packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:230 — drive-by change of the user-facing string 'Notes have been hidden by the organiser' → 'organizer' in the hideCalendarNotes path, unrelated to this PR and capable of breaking tests/snapshots asserting the previous wording.

[Medium/test_gap] The only test change is a single e2e snapshot literal (`destinationCalendar: null` → `[]`); there is no coverage for the new multi-destination collective creation, credentialId-based calendar selection in GoogleCalendarService, cancel/update with multiple calendar references, or the broken fallbacks (issues 2, 4, 5, 6) — all paths this PR rewrites.

goldens.comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.

Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled

The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts updateEvent (~253) and deleteEvent (~315) — the fallback `destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is only evaluated in the branch where externalCalendarId is falsy, so the predicate never matches; calendarId/selectedCalendar becomes undefined and googleapis rejects the call with 'Missing required parameter: calendarId', breaking update/delete for references with null/absent externalCalendarId (legacy bookings and the new no-credentialId path).

adjudication.rationale: In packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts, both updateEvent and deleteEvent now compute the calendar id as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the else-branch), the predicate compares against that same falsy value, so it will not match any normal `DestinationCalendar.externalId` and returns `undefined` instead of falling back to a destination calendar’s externalId (previously `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`). This is a real logic regression introduced by the diff and can lead to an undefined/incorrect calendarId being used for update/delete when `externalCalendarId` is missing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:~145-155 — `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"` silently creates the event on the credential's primary calendar when no destinationCalendar entry matches credentialId, causing duplicate events for multi-credential users or events on the wrong account when destination rows have null credentialId; additionally CalendarManager.createEvent echoes back the passed-in externalId even when 'primary' was actually used, so the stored reference points at the wrong calendar.

adjudication.rationale: In `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent`, `selectedCalendar` is derived only via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`, and the insert uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`. If no destination calendar entry matches the given `credentialId` (e.g., destination rows have `credentialId` null/undefined or mismatched), the event will be created on the credential’s primary calendar, which is a behavior change that can place events on the wrong calendar/account. Additionally, `CalendarManager.createEvent` now returns `{ externalId }` from its parameter (passed from `EventManager` as `destination.externalId`) regardless of whether Google actually fell back to `primary`, so the resulting stored reference can point to an external calendar id that was not used.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] Office365 CalendarService (72-76), Lark CalendarService (127-129), and packages/lib/CalendarService.ts (156-163) — these services read only `destinationCalendar[0].externalId` and ignore the per-credential entry (credentialId param unused), so in the multi-host collective flow each host's credential writes to the first host's calendar externalId causing API errors/404s; the collective multiple host feature effectively only works with Google.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `destinationCalendar` to an array and introduces per-credential selection for Google (`GoogleCalendarService.createEvent(calEventRaw, credentialId)` and `.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`), but Office365 and Lark still destructure only the first entry (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []; const calendarId = mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId;`) and do not use a `credentialId` to select the matching destination calendar. Similarly, `packages/lib/CalendarService.ts` now filters calendars using only `destinationCalendar[0].externalId`, which will incorrectly constrain operations when multiple destination calendars exist. In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, the same `event` object (with the full destinationCalendar array) is passed for each host/credential, so non-Google services will target the first host’s externalId rather than the per-credential one, matching the finding’s described failure mode for collective multi-host.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] packages/core/EventManager.ts:~377-385 — in createAllCalendarEvents, the no-credentialId else branch (filter by integration type + create on every matching credential) now runs once per destination inside the for loop, so two destination entries with the same integration and null credentialId create N×M duplicate events.

adjudication.rationale: In packages/core/EventManager.ts `createAllCalendarEvents`, the refactor changes destinationCalendar to an array and iterates `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)`. In the `else` branch when `destination.credentialId` is falsy, it computes `destinationCalendarCredentials = this.calendarCredentials.filter((c) => c.type === destination.integration)` and then appends `Promise.all(destinationCalendarCredentials.map(async (c) => await createEvent(c, event)))`. Because this branch is inside the loop, multiple `destination` entries with the same `integration` and no `credentialId` will each trigger creation across the same matching credentials, producing duplicate events (N destinations × M credentials). This duplication behavior is directly implied by the new loop structure in the diff.

This matches the golden comment’s concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] packages/core/EventManager.ts:~552-555 — the newBookingId merge cleanup uses `booking.references.find((reference) => reference.type.includes("_calendar"))` and deletes only the first old calendar reference, so reschedule/merge on bookings created via the multi-destination flow leaves stale events on the other hosts' calendars.

adjudication.rationale: In packages/core/EventManager.ts, updateCalendarEvent now collects multiple calendar references via `filter((reference) => reference.type.includes("_calendar"))` and updates them in a loop. However, the merge-cleanup block for `newBookingId` still uses `const oldCalendarEvent = booking.references.find((reference) => reference.type.includes("_calendar"));`, which will delete at most one old calendar event reference even if the booking has multiple `_calendar` references (as introduced by the multi-destination changes). This can leave stale events on other destination calendars.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:~440-470 — the recurring-series deletion block (iterating all of bookingToDelete.user.credentials × updatedBookings, ignoring the loop's reference) is now inside the `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop, executing once per calendar reference causing duplicate delete calls and repeated 404/log noise; it also still only covers the organizer's credentials so other hosts' recurring events are never cleaned up.

adjudication.rationale: In handleCancelBooking.ts the recurring-series deletion block is now nested inside `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` (after switching from `.find` to `.filter`). That block loops over `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` and `updatedBookings` and does not depend on the current `reference`, so if there are multiple `_calendar` references it will execute multiple times and enqueue duplicate `deleteEvent` calls (likely causing repeated 404s/log noise). The claim about only using the organizer’s credentials is also supported by the code: it exclusively iterates `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` and does not consider other hosts’ credentials.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/data] packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:~1871-1877 — only `evt.destinationCalendar[0]` is connected to the booking and there is no schema migration to persist per-host destinations, so later flows that rebuild CalendarEvent from booking.destinationCalendar (confirm.handler.ts, paypal-webhook.ts, webhook.ts handlePaymentSuccess) create calendar events only on the first host's calendar, silently skipping all other hosts' destination calendars for collective bookings requiring payment/confirmation.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and, for COLLECTIVE team events, explicitly appends additional host destination calendars (`evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);` in `handleNewBooking.ts`). However, when persisting the booking, it only connects the first destination calendar (`connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }`), dropping the rest. Subsequent flows shown in the diff (e.g., `confirm.handler.ts`, `paypal-webhook.ts`, `webhook.ts`) rebuild `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` from `booking.destinationCalendar` (singular) into a single-element array, so they can only act on the persisted first calendar and will miss the other hosts’ calendars for post-booking actions (payment/confirmation).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/security] packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:~755-760 — loadUsers' catch rethrows Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError messages verbatim as a 400 response, leaking internal database error details to API clients and miscategorizing a server-side failure as a client error.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `loadUsers` in `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts` was changed to wrap its logic in a `try/catch` and, on `Prisma.PrismaClientKnownRequestError`, it throws `new HttpError({ statusCode: 400, message: error.message })`. This both (a) returns Prisma’s internal error message verbatim to the client (information disclosure) and (b) reports a server-side DB failure as a 400 client error. This behavior is explicitly present in the added catch block.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/requestReschedule.handler.ts:239-242 — the original duplicated expression (`bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar || bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar`, missing the intended `|| user.destinationCalendar`) is preserved as `? [bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar] : []` instead of adding the user fallback used consistently in every other handler converted in this PR.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/requestReschedule.handler.ts`, the pre-existing duplicated fallback (`bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar || bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar`) is “fixed” to only use `bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar ? [bookingToReschedule?.destinationCalendar] : []` (lines shown in the diff), but unlike other updated handlers in this PR (e.g. `confirm.handler.ts`, `editLocation.handler.ts`, payments/webhooks) it does not fall back to the booking user’s `destinationCalendar` when the booking has none. This can result in an empty `destinationCalendar` array for reschedule requests where a user default calendar exists, changing behavior versus the rest of the codebase and likely the intended behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:230 — drive-by change of the user-facing string 'Notes have been hidden by the organiser' → 'organizer' in the hideCalendarNotes path, unrelated to this PR and capable of breaking tests/snapshots asserting the previous wording.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change the literal user-facing string in packages/core/CalendarManager.ts from "Notes have been hidden by the organiser" to "Notes have been hidden by the organizer" in the hideCalendarNotes path. This is unrelated to the surrounding destinationCalendar refactor and could cause snapshot/string-assertion test churn, but it’s not inherently a functional defect (just wording/locale change).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] The only test change is a single e2e snapshot literal (`destinationCalendar: null` → `[]`); there is no coverage for the new multi-destination collective creation, credentialId-based calendar selection in GoogleCalendarService, cancel/update with multiple calendar references, or the broken fallbacks (issues 2, 4, 5, 6) — all paths this PR rewrites.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows substantial behavioral refactors (e.g., `destinationCalendar` becomes an array across types and call sites; EventManager now loops over multiple destination calendars and multiple `_calendar` references; GoogleCalendarService `createEvent` now takes `credentialId` and selects calendar via `destinationCalendar.find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`; cancel/update paths now handle `references.filter(...)` and iterate). Yet the only visible test adjustment is in `apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts` changing `destinationCalendar: null` to `destinationCalendar: []`. No other tests are added/updated here to exercise the new multi-destination collective behavior (`handleNewBooking` pushing team calendars), credentialId-based selection, or multi-reference update/cancel logic. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test coverage concern for newly introduced complex logic rather than a directly verifiable runtime defect.
